cases.text: Hãy chạy bộ unit test trong thư mục 'tests/' để tìm các lỗi ZeroDivisionError và KeyError trong file 'app.py', sau đó sửa lại mã nguồn trong 'app.py' sao cho toàn bộ unit test đều PASS.
Chạy thử bộ unit test trong thư mục 'tests/' và sửa lỗi KeyError khi trường 'id' bị thiếu trong dữ liệu JSON tại file 'src/data_parser.py'.
Hãy kiểm tra và sửa lỗi cú pháp trong file 'calculator.py' để hàm add(a, b) hoạt động bình thường.
Sửa lỗi NameError trong file 'math_utils.py' do dùng hàm math.sqrt mà chưa import thư viện math.
Bổ sung kiểm tra null cho biến user trong file 'UserService.java' để tránh lỗi NullPointerException khi gọi getName().
Dọn dẹp các ký hiệu xung đột Git (<<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>) trong file 'config.py' và giữ lại giá trị PORT = 8080.

Design a system where an LLM-based assistant can autonomously manage a small e-commerce store's customer support: it should triage incoming tickets by intent (refund, tracking, product question, complaint), decide when to escalate to a human, use tools like an order lookup API and a refund processing API, and handle multi-turn conversations where it might need to gather info across several steps before resolving an issue. I want the full architecture—how the agent loop works, what the tool schemas look like, how memory/state is maintained between turns, and how you'd implement guardrails so it doesn't approve refunds above a certain threshold without human approval. Please include pseudocode for the core orchestration logic.

Design a lobby screen for ShieldBattery that displays while players are waiting for a match to start — it should show each player's race selection, their MMR badge, a real-time countdown timer, and a map preview with spawn locations highlighted. I want the layout to feel bold and confident, not like a generic loading screen — think strong typography, dramatic use of negative space, and maybe some subtle animated accents that reinforce the competitive atmosphere without being distracting. Can you build this out as a React component using the existing design system tokens?

Here's the landing page for my poetry journal's website — the text is all over the place right now. The heading uses Papyrus, the body copy is in 11px Arial, the author bylines are bold italic 18px while the poem titles are regular 12px, and the pull quotes are the same size as everything else so nothing stands out. Can you rework the CSS so the typographic hierarchy actually makes sense — proper font pairings, consistent weights, readable sizes, and clear visual distinction between headings, poem titles, bylines, body text, and featured quotes?

Set up a Claude Code hook system in TypeScript that intercepts every shell command execution, checks it against a configurable allowlist/blocklist of patterns (e.g., block `rm -rf /`, allow `npm test`), and either permits or rejects the command with a logged reason. I want shared utility modules for pattern matching and config loading, the whole thing compiled with esbuild so only JS gets distributed to teammates, and a full Vitest test suite covering edge cases like glob patterns, empty configs, and concurrent hook invocations.

Design a Python-based research assistant that can answer multi-step scientific questions by autonomously deciding which tools to use (web search, arxiv API, Python REPL for calculations, and a citation database), planning a sequence of actions, executing them, reflecting on intermediate results to decide next steps, and synthesizing a final answer with sources — include the orchestration loop, tool definitions, memory/state management between steps, and error recovery when a tool call fails or returns irrelevant results.

We're preparing for our Series B board meeting next week and I need help with three things. First, our CEO wants a strategic framework for presenting two acquisition scenarios to the board — one where we acquire a competitor for $12M and another where we organically grow into their market over 18 months — including projected revenue impact and how to frame the risk/reward for our lead investor who's been skeptical about M&A. Second, we just had a professional photographer shoot our new executive team portraits for the investor deck and annual report; I've attached the five finalist shots and need a detailed composition and aesthetic analysis of each to help us pick the one that projects the most confidence and approachability for stakeholder-facing materials. Third, our investor-facing product demo portal (built in Next.js) keeps breaking before board meetings — can you write a comprehensive Playwright end-to-end test suite that covers the login flow, the live metrics dashboard, the financial projections interactive charts, and the scenario comparison tool, so we can run automated checks the morning of every board presentation and catch regressions before any director sees a broken page?

We're building an internal "intelligent code review" microservice that uses an LLM to automatically summarize pull requests and flag potential security issues across our monorepo (~2M lines of Python/Go). Before I write up the formal decision doc, I need help with three things: (1) Search our codebase semantically for all places where we're already doing any kind of AI-powered analysis, static analysis hooks, or LLM API calls — I know there are at least a couple experiments scattered around but grep for "openai" only catches some of them, I need a conceptual search for anything doing automated code understanding or summarization regardless of which provider or library it uses. (2) Based on what we find, write an ADR for choosing between calling a hosted API (GPT-4o / Claude) vs. deploying a fine-tuned open model (CodeLlama or StarCoder2) with LoRA adapters on our existing k8s GPU nodes — the ADR should weigh latency, cost at our PR volume (~400/day), data privacy since we can't send proprietary code externally without legal review, and evaluate whether RAG over our style guides would be sufficient vs. actually fine-tuning on our historical review comments. (3) Sketch out the evaluation pipeline for the LLM component — how we'd build a golden dataset from past reviewer comments, what metrics to track (hallucination rate on code references, agreement with human reviewers, false positive rate on security flags), and how we'd set up an A/B rollout with cost guardrails before going org-wide.

We have raw Stripe payment data landing in our warehouse and I need to build out the full dbt model chain for it. Start with a staging model (`stg_stripe__payments`) that renames and casts the columns from the `raw.stripe.payments` source — use the standard CTE pattern with an `source` CTE, a `renamed` CTE, and a final select. Then build an intermediate model (`int_payments_pivoted_to_orders`) that aggregates payments by order, pivoting payment methods into separate amount columns, and finally a marts model (`fct_orders`) that joins the intermediate payment model with `stg_jaffle_shop__orders` to produce a clean fact table with order-level revenue metrics. Make sure each model follows the right conventions for its layer — ephemeral for intermediate, table for marts, proper ref usage, and include a `_dbt_utils.surrogate_key` where appropriate.

Our UniFi network spans 14 sites across three regional offices, and over the past year different team members have created separate markdown files documenting host inventories, device configs, VLAN assignments, and troubleshooting runbooks — but there's massive overlap and contradiction between them. I need you to first pull a current inventory of all hosts and devices across every UniFi site so we have an accurate baseline of what's actually deployed (include status, model, firmware, IP, and which site each belongs to), then take the 23 documentation files in our `/docs/infrastructure/` folder and consolidate them into a clean, non-redundant set. Merge the VLAN docs (there are four covering nearly the same content), combine the three overlapping troubleshooting guides, and unify the per-site inventory docs into one canonical source-of-truth document that reflects the live infrastructure data you just pulled. Make sure nothing valuable gets lost — some files have unique notes about firmware quirks or site-specific firewall rules that only appear once — but eliminate all the duplicated and outdated content.

We're setting up a Pharo Smalltalk project for a legacy insurance calculation engine and I need two things done. First, generate an AGENTS.md and AI configuration files for the repo so that any AI assistant working on it knows the project conventions — it's a Tonel-format Pharo 11 project, tests live under `InsuranceEngine-Tests`, and we follow the `on:do:` pattern for all exception handling rather than letting things bubble up. Second, I'm stuck on a failing test: `InsurancePremiumCalculatorTest>>testRiskAdjustment` is throwing a `MessageNotUnderstood: UndefinedObject>>*` somewhere in the calculation chain, and when I try to step through it in the debugger the UI just hangs — I suspect it's hitting an infinite loop in one of the lookup methods. The stack trace shows it going through `RiskProfile>>adjustedFactor` → `PolicyHolder>>riskCategory` → `RiskTable>>at:` which then seems to return nil instead of a numeric value. Can you help me systematically debug this (maybe execute the methods incrementally to inspect intermediate values) and also make sure the AGENTS.md captures our debugging workflow and Smalltalk-specific conventions so future contributors know how to handle these kinds of issues?

We have a suite of AILANG teaching prompts that guide our PostgreSQL monitoring system's instance actors on how to respond to various health check scenarios (connection pool exhaustion, replication lag, long-running queries, etc.). Two problems: first, several of the prompts have ballooned to 3-4x their original token count with redundant instructions and outdated examples, so I need them trimmed down and restructured for maximum conciseness while preserving accuracy — especially the prompts covering failover detection and WAL archiving checks. Second, we're seeing three instance actors stuck in a stale state on our `pg-prod-replica-03` node — they haven't reported health metrics in over 6 hours and the orchestration logs show them looping on an authentication retry. Can you help me optimize those AILANG prompts (I'll paste them below) and also walk me through diagnosing and restarting those stale actors so they resume proper health monitoring?

We're building a developer education platform and I need help with three interconnected pieces. First, I'm creating a Zed editor extension in Rust that provides a custom `/webinar-notes` slash command — when invoked during a live coding webinar, it should pull the current webinar's agenda, talking points, and audience poll results from our Firestore backend and format them as contextual notes in the editor. The slash command needs to output structured markdown with engagement hooks (audience questions to pose, demo transition cues, and "aha moment" callouts) so the presenter can glance at it while live-coding. For the Firestore side, I need an async service layer in TypeScript that manages webinar documents (agenda items, real-time poll results, attendee engagement scores) with transactions to atomically update the engagement metrics as audience members interact, plus proper error handling for when the presenter's extension polls during high-traffic moments. The webinar narrative itself needs to build toward a climactic live refactoring demo — help me structure the arc so it starts with a relatable "legacy code pain" story, builds tension through incremental improvements, includes two interactive polling moments to keep the audience engaged, and lands on a satisfying reveal. Show me the full Rust extension code with the `run_slash_command` implementation, the Firestore service with transaction patterns, and the webinar flow document that ties them together.

Create a skill called "django-test-runner" that sets up a Django project scaffold with pytest configuration, factory_boy fixtures, and coverage reporting — it should generate the models, views, serializers, and corresponding test files for a basic blog API (posts, comments, tags). Package the whole thing up as a proper skill with a complete README, push it to a new branch on our GitHub repo at github.com/ourteam/django-utils, open a PR with a detailed description of what the skill does, and then verify I can pull it down locally by downloading and checking that all the generated files are present and the test suite actually passes.

We're launching a new internal developer portal (React frontend, Go microservices, PostgreSQL) and I need two things done together. First, generate a comprehensive PRD for the portal — it should cover user authentication via SSO, a service catalog, API documentation browser, and an environment provisioning self-service module. Make sure the PRD is structured for task breakdown with clear acceptance criteria, and run all your validation checks against it. Once the PRD passes, go ahead and break it into tasks with dependency tracking and datetime estimates. Second, before any tasks start executing, I need a full CI/CD pipeline designed alongside it: GitHub Actions workflows for the Go services (unit tests, golangci-lint, Trivy container scanning, and multi-stage Docker builds pushing to ECR), a separate workflow for the React app (Jest + Playwright tests, npm audit, S3/CloudFront deploy), plus a shared reusable workflow for database migrations with approval gates before prod. I want canary deployments for the Go services using ArgoCD with automatic rollback if error rates exceed 1%. The pipeline definitions should be included as infrastructure tasks in the PRD's task breakdown so everything is sequenced correctly — like the CI pipeline tasks need to be completed before any deployment-related feature tasks can begin. If anything in the PRD validation fails, I want to be able to roll back to the generation step rather than manually patching.

I have a 120,000-word historical fiction manuscript set during the French Revolution, and I need a comprehensive dramatic function analysis of every major plot point across all 42 chapters. The novel interweaves three POV characters — a noblewoman, a revolutionary, and a priest — and I'm struggling to see where the dramatic tension sags and where subplots fail to converge. Can you preprocess the full text to identify all major plot points per chapter, then analyze each one in parallel across the three storylines for its dramatic function (inciting incident, rising action, reversal, climax, resolution, etc.), track how dramatic stakes escalate or plateau across the arc, and finally integrate everything into a structured report that maps out the dramatic rhythm of the whole novel? I especially need to see where plot points across the three POVs should be creating dramatic irony or thematic resonance but currently aren't, and where the pacing between chapters 18–27 loses momentum. The final report should include a chapter-by-chapter dramatic function table, a tension curve visualization description, and specific revision recommendations.

Our grid modernization team just submitted a paper to IEEE PES General Meeting on using physics-guided self-supervised GNNs for cascading failure prediction in transmission networks. Before the camera-ready deadline, I need two things done simultaneously: (1) Do a thorough technical review of the manuscript — validate that our power flow equations and line flow constraints are physically consistent, check whether our cascade simulation claims are properly supported by the experimental evidence in Tables 3-5, audit Figures 7 and 8 for correct axis labels and statistical significance markers, compare our results against the PPGT baseline fairly, and flag any IEEE formatting compliance issues. (2) Using the key findings and reviewer-ready summary from that analysis, package a 5-slide executive briefing for our VP of Engineering and the CTO that covers the strategic significance of this research for our utility's reliability program, the decision on whether to fund Phase 2 field validation, and a one-page decision log capturing the technical risks identified during the review. The board meets Thursday so the deck needs to translate the ML and power systems jargon into business impact language.

Our e-commerce team is running a big summer promo across our DTC site, Amazon, and retail partners — I need a full merchandising plan covering the hero banner placements on our homepage, category page feature slots, email cadence, and channel-specific discount tiers for the 3-week campaign. At the same time, our deploy pipeline for the promo landing pages is broken — the GitHub Actions workflow `deploy-promo-pages.yml` has been failing on the `build-and-test` job for the last 4 runs with what looks like a Node memory issue or a flaky integration test, and I need you to pull the run logs, diagnose the root cause, and suggest a fix so we can actually ship the page updates. Finally, the promo pages are powered by a Strands-based AI agent that generates personalized product recommendations for each visitor, and we need to wire up Langfuse tracing on that agent so we can monitor latency, token costs, and recommendation quality in production throughout the campaign — walk me through the full OpenTelemetry integration with Langfuse for our Strands agent and make sure we have dashboards ready before launch day.

Our React dashboard for the internal HR portal has accumulated a lot of technical debt over the past year — inconsistent component patterns, accessibility issues, missing dark mode support, and several modules that bypass our design system entirely. I need you to do a full quality audit of the codebase (it's at `github.com/acmecorp/hr-portal`), identify every issue across code quality, UI consistency, and accessibility, then file each finding as a GitHub issue with severity labels and PM-prioritized recommendations. After that, for the highest-priority UI issue you find, go ahead and build a fixed version of the component using shadcn/ui and Tailwind with proper responsive breakpoints, dark mode tokens, and ARIA attributes, then open a pull request with a conventional commit title like `fix(ui): rebuild EmployeeCard with accessible shadcn/ui primitives` so we can start reviewing immediately. I want the audit, the issues, and at least that first PR all done in one pass.

I'm building a math-themed board game in Obsidian where two players take turns placing pieces on a hex grid to claim territory — no dice, no hidden info, pure strategy like Go meets Hex. I need three things: First, help me design the core mechanics, win conditions, and balance considerations so neither player has an overwhelming first-move advantage. Second, I want to visualize the scoring function for territory control as interactive Desmos graphs embedded in my Obsidian notes — specifically, I need parametric curves showing how the value of connected regions grows nonlinearly with size, and inequality shading to represent each player's dominated zones on a coordinate plane approximation of the board. Third, I want the game to have a soundtrack feature: write me an AppleScript that queries my Apple Music library for tracks in a "Board Games" playlist, shuffles them, and starts playback when I launch the game session, with the ability to shift to a different playlist called "Endgame Tension" when a player controls more than 60% of the board — I'll trigger that manually from a hotkey. Can you put together the game design document, the Desmos graph code blocks, and the AppleScript all in one cohesive Obsidian note?

Build me a reusable notification toast component in React that supports success, error, warning, and info variants. Each variant should have distinct colors, icons, and an optional progress bar for auto-dismiss timing. I want it styled entirely with Tailwind CSS using a custom design token system (e.g., `--color-success-50` through `--color-success-900` for each semantic color) so the palette can be swapped via a single theme config. Use shadcn/ui's patterns for composability — separate `ToastProvider`, `Toast`, `ToastTitle`, `ToastDescription`, and `ToastAction` primitives. Make sure the focus ring styles, color contrast ratios, and aria-live regions pass WCAG 2.1 AA. Also add responsive behavior so toasts stack differently on mobile (bottom full-width) vs desktop (top-right corner with max-width), and show me how to configure the Tailwind `theme.extend` block to register the custom tokens properly.

Build me a Swift package for a multi-tenant document management API on Apple's new Foundation Models framework. Each tenant has roles (admin, editor, viewer) and document-level attribute policies (e.g., department match, clearance level, time-based access windows). I want a `DocumentAccessController` that combines RBAC role checks with ABAC attribute evaluation so that, for example, an editor can only modify documents in their own department during business hours. On top of that, integrate a `LanguageModelSession` with a custom `@Generable` struct for document summaries — when a user requests a summary of a document they're authorized to view, the system should use a `@Guide`-annotated enum to constrain the summary style (brief, detailed, executive), call the session to generate it via streaming, and enforce that unauthorized users get a proper denial before the LLM is ever invoked. Include a `Tool` conformance that lets the model look up related documents the user is permitted to see, respecting the same RBAC+ABAC policies. Show the full implementation with tests covering role hierarchy overrides, attribute policy edge cases, and the streaming generation flow.

We have the TMF641 Service Ordering API spec (TMF641-ServiceOrdering-v4.1.0.swagger.json) and need to stand up an MCP server from it. Please parse the OpenAPI YAML, generate tool definitions for each operation (GET /serviceOrder, POST /serviceOrder, PATCH /serviceOrder/{id}, DELETE /serviceOrder/{id}, plus the /hub and /listener endpoints for event subscriptions), resolve all the $ref and allOf schemas into flat input models, apply the standard TMF tool naming convention (e.g. `tmf641_create_service_order`, `tmf641_retrieve_service_order`), produce a lightweight mock Express server that returns valid example payloads for each endpoint, and wire up a corresponding MCP server that exposes every operation as an invocable tool with proper JSON Schema inputs. Make sure the /hub registration tool follows the standard TMF event-subscription pattern so downstream consumers can subscribe to `ServiceOrderCreateEvent` and `ServiceOrderStateChangeEvent` notifications.

Our ABP-based microservices platform processes physics simulation jobs where each job's state is modeled using Gay.jl's bisimulation game framework — we derive GF(3) trit values from hue-based color encodings of simulation states, and these trits must satisfy conservation laws across service boundaries. Right now we have three services: `SimulationOrchestrator`, `StateResolver`, and `BillingService`. When a simulation completes, `SimulationOrchestrator` publishes a `SimulationCompletedEto` that both other services consume. The problem is threefold: (1) `StateResolver` sometimes processes the same event twice during pod restarts, causing duplicate bisimulation game evaluations and breaking GF(3) conservation invariants on the derived trit sequences — I need idempotent event handlers that check whether a given game's trit derivation has already been committed before recomputing. (2) We run multi-tenant and some simulation jobs are cross-tenant collaborations, so the completed event needs to fan out to `BillingService` handlers in both tenant contexts while preserving the hue-to-trit mapping consistency per tenant's color space configuration. (3) The whole pipeline — from simulation completion through state resolution to billing — needs to be orchestrated as a saga so that if the Gay.jl bisimulation verification fails conservation checks, we compensate the billing charge and requeue the simulation. I also need you to spin up a coordinator agent that monitors these saga executions autonomously: it should pick up failed sagas from a GitHub issue queue, attempt automated retriage by re-running the GF(3) conservation validation, and flag any that need my manual approval before compensating. Set up the approval workflow so I can review and approve/reject each compensation via PR comments. Can you design the full event topology, the idempotent handler pattern with the bisimulation trit checks, the cross-tenant event routing, the saga with compensation, and the coordinator daemon configuration?

Hey, I just finished the database migration refactoring that's been tracked in our todo.md as "Migrate user_sessions table to new schema with partitioning support." Can you mark that task as done in todo.md (remove it from the active tasks list) and add a corresponding entry in changelog.md under today's date noting the completion? Make sure both files are updated in a single atomic operation so we don't end up with one reflecting the change and the other not if something interrupts.

Our PostgreSQL cluster (primary + 2 replicas) running on Kubernetes handles all transaction data for our fintech platform, and we need a bulletproof automated backup and disaster recovery setup. Write me a comprehensive backup strategy that includes: (1) a CronJob manifest that runs `pg_basebackup` for full weekly backups and WAL archiving for continuous point-in-time recovery to an S3-compatible object store, (2) a shell script that validates backup integrity by spinning up a temporary Pod, restoring the latest backup, running checksums against the live database, and reporting pass/fail to our Slack webhook, (3) a documented runbook for the restore procedure covering both full cluster failover and single-table recovery scenarios with exact `pg_restore` and `pg_waldump` commands, and (4) a Terraform module that provisions the S3 bucket with lifecycle policies to rotate out backups older than 90 days. We had an incident last quarter where a backup turned out to be corrupted and nobody noticed for three weeks, so I want the validation piece to be especially robust — test row counts on critical tables, verify WAL continuity, and alert immediately on any gaps.

How do I use the `b2c` CLI to register a new SLAS client for our storefront, configure the callback URIs for both our staging and production environments, and then retrieve the client credentials so I can plug them into our Commerce Cloud API integration? Also, if there's a way to list all existing SLAS clients to make sure we're not duplicating registrations, walk me through that too.

Set up a new Deepnote workspace for our InsightPulseAI data team that organizes notebooks into exploration, scheduled ETL jobs, and Superset-ready summary table sections. We need a shared project configuration that includes pre-commit security hooks to prevent credential leaks, a standardized Claude-based framework structure for each notebook template, and auto-detection logic so the setup script can identify whether a notebook is using PySpark, pandas, or SQL-only and apply the right boilerplate accordingly. The summary tables should land in a `gold/` schema that Superset can query directly, and each job notebook needs a consistent header block with dataset lineage metadata. Can you generate the full setup scaffolding and the detection patterns for this?

Our mid-size 3PL company handles warehousing and last-mile delivery for about 40 e-commerce brands across the US. We're losing margins because every client has different SLA requirements, return handling workflows, and carrier preferences, and our ops team is stitching everything together manually in spreadsheets. I need you to design a comprehensive automation playbook that maps out the key pain points in our fulfillment pipeline — from order ingestion and inventory sync through pick/pack/ship to returns processing and client billing — and recommends specific workflow automations we can bundle as tiered service offerings (Basic, Pro, Enterprise) for our e-commerce clients. For each tier, outline which integrations (Shopify/WooCommerce webhooks, carrier APIs, WMS triggers) should be automated versus manual, how to handle exception flows like address corrections and split shipments, and what KPI dashboards each client tier gets access to. Also include a section on how we can adapt the same playbook framework for our newer professional services clients (accounting firms and law offices) who use us for document storage and courier delivery, since their compliance and chain-of-custody requirements are completely different from e-commerce fulfillment.

Our patient portal's appointment scheduling page (React + TypeScript) works perfectly but looks like it was designed in 2012. I'm attaching the full component below — it has a complex flow with insurance verification hooks, real-time provider availability polling via WebSocket, optimistic UI updates for slot reservations, and a multi-step form with Formik/Yup validation that feeds into our FHIR-compliant backend. I need you to give it a complete visual overhaul — think clean, modern, Apple Health or One Medical level aesthetics with smooth transitions, generous whitespace, subtle shadows, refined typography, and a calming color palette. The scheduling calendar, provider cards, insurance verification status indicators, and confirmation summary all need to feel premium and trustworthy. But please don't touch any of the booking logic, the WebSocket subscription in `useProviderAvailability`, the insurance verification mutation, or the Formik form submission handler — every single hook, API call, and state update must remain exactly as-is. Just make it beautiful.

Our team inherited a Go gRPC service for an internal order fulfillment system and nobody who originally built it is still around. The repo has about 15 `.proto` files under `proto/fulfillment/v1/`, service implementations in `internal/server/`, and a bunch of interceptors in `pkg/middleware/`. Can you walk me through the overall architecture — map out which proto services exist, how they relate to each other, which RPCs use streaming vs unary, what the interceptor chain does (auth, logging, rate limiting, etc.), and flag any anti-patterns you see in how the server-side handlers are implemented? Also, we noticed some RPCs seem to pass around huge nested messages that duplicate fields from other messages, so call out any proto design issues. Finally, generate a markdown API reference doc for each service that includes the RPC signatures, message schemas, streaming types, and the middleware that applies to each endpoint.

Here's the landing page for our literary magazine's annual submission call — it's a single HTML/CSS file. The text is all over the place right now: the heading and subheading are both the same size, body copy uses a system default sans-serif while pull quotes use Comic Sans for some reason, the font weights are inconsistent (some paragraphs are bold for no reason, others are too light to read), and the line-height on the submission guidelines section makes it feel super cramped. Can you go through the whole file and make the typography cohesive and polished? I want a clear visual hierarchy from the page title down through section headers to body text, readable line spacing, consistent weights, and font choices that feel appropriate for a literary publication. Keep the existing HTML structure but fix all the CSS typography issues.

Our startup just closed a Series B and I'm preparing for next week's board meeting where I need to present our updated go-to-market strategy and 18-month financial projections with three scenario models (conservative/base/aggressive). The board also wants to see our investor relations roadmap for the next fundraising cycle. Separately, we're revamping our company's visual brand — our head of marketing submitted five candidate hero images for the new homepage and investor deck cover, and I need a detailed composition and aesthetic critique of each photo (I'll share them) evaluating things like rule of thirds, color harmony, visual weight distribution, and overall NIMA-style aesthetic scoring so we can pick the strongest one for both web and print. Finally, the homepage where these hero images will live is a Next.js app and we need a full Playwright end-to-end test suite covering the homepage hero carousel (autoplay, swipe, pause on hover, responsive breakpoints across Chrome/Firefox/WebKit), the investor portal login flow behind it, and the scenario toggle on the public financial summary page that switches between the three projection models — please use Page Object Model and include visual regression snapshots for each carousel slide.

We're designing an embedded HTTP server for our IoT gateway firmware using Rust 2024 edition, and I'd like your help writing the core request router. It should use a trie-based route table that supports path parameters (e.g., `/devices/{id}/telemetry`), async handler functions (using the new async closures from edition 2024), and a middleware pipeline with composable layers for auth, logging, and rate limiting. I want the design to be fully `#[deny(clippy::all, clippy::pedantic, clippy::nursery)]` clean, use zero heap allocations in the hot path via arena allocation, and leverage the new `gen` blocks for streaming response bodies. Please include the module structure, the core types with full doc comments following RFC 1574 conventions, and a benchmark-friendly example showing how to register routes and compose middleware. Also show how you'd handle graceful shutdown with cancellation safety using `tokio::select!` and the new pin ergonomics.

Our ML platform team is building a customer support automation system and I need help across three areas. First, search our codebase (it's a Python monorepo under `src/`) for any existing implementations or patterns related to retrieval-augmented generation, embedding pipelines, vector store integrations, and prompt template management — I want a conceptual map of what we already have before making new decisions. Second, based on what you find, write an ADR for our decision on whether to use a pure prompting approach with structured few-shot examples, a RAG pipeline backed by our existing Elasticsearch cluster plus a vector store, or fine-tuning/LoRA on our labeled ticket-resolution dataset (~120k examples). The ADR should weigh latency requirements (p95 < 2s), our current infra constraints (we're on GCP with a commitment through 2026, running GKE, and have budget approval for 2xA100 nodes), model hosting costs for the candidates we're evaluating (Claude via API, Llama 3 70B self-hosted, Mistral via La Plateforme), accuracy targets against our eval suite, and data privacy concerns since tickets contain PII. Third, for whichever approach the ADR recommends, outline the full implementation plan including dataset preparation and filtering, evaluation methodology (I want both automated metrics and an LLM-as-judge pipeline with inter-annotator agreement tracking), a prompt versioning strategy, guardrails for hallucination and cost controls, and a phased rollout from shadow mode to production with human-in-the-loop escalation paths.

We're rebuilding our analytics warehouse in dbt and I need help structuring the models for our e-commerce order funnel. We have raw tables `raw.shopify_orders`, `raw.shopify_order_line_items`, `raw.stripe_payments`, and `raw.shipstation_shipments` landing in our Snowflake warehouse via Fivetran. I need you to write out the full dbt SQL files for: (1) staging models for each source with proper renaming, type casting, and deduplication, (2) an intermediate model `int_orders_with_payments` that joins orders to their payment records using a CTE pattern that keeps the logic readable, and (3) a mart model `fct_order_performance` that brings everything together and calculates metrics like gross revenue, net revenue after refunds, average fulfillment time, and a flag for orders where payment was received but shipment took longer than 5 business days. We're building a browser-based music visualizer in TypeScript and I need help designing and implementing the particle engine that drives it. Each particle needs proper physics: velocity integration, configurable drag so they don't fly off forever, and soft-body collision against the viewport edges with energy loss on bounce. I also want an "attractor mode" where clicking the canvas places a gravity well that particles orbit around with realistic falloff. The whole thing needs to run at 60fps with 10k+ particles, so I'm thinking about using a spatial hash for neighbor lookups and doing the force accumulation in a single pass. Before we start coding, I'd like you to brainstorm the architecture — break down the force pipeline, figure out the right integration method (Euler vs Verlet for this use case), plan out the data structures for the spatial partitioning, and create a detailed implementation checklist with todos we can track as we build each module. We have a Rust service that processes financial transactions through a pipeline of validation stages — parsing, normalization, enrichment, risk scoring, and finally settlement routing. I want to refactor the entire pipeline so that data can only flow forward in a valid state — meaning each stage's output type *guarantees* the invariants the next stage requires, making it structurally impossible to pass unvalidated or partially-processed transactions between stages. Can you help me redesign the type hierarchy and stage boundaries using Rust's type system (newtypes, typestate pattern, etc.) so the compiler itself enforces that data follows the correct path through the pipeline, invalid states are unrepresentable, and every error is surfaced at the exact stage it originates rather than corrupting downstream consumers? Show me the core type definitions, the stage function signatures, and explain the design principles behind why each boundary is drawn where it is.
